00001| """Retry policies for failed job attempts.
00002| 
00003| A :class:`RetryPolicy` answers two questions the scheduler asks whenever an
00004| attempt fails:
00005| 
00006| 1. *Should we try again?* -- :meth:`RetryPolicy.should_retry`, given how many
00007|    attempts have already been made.
00008| 2. *If so, how long until the next attempt?* -- :meth:`RetryPolicy.next_delay`,
00009|    a virtual-time delay derived from the configured backoff strategy.
00010| 
00011| Both are pure functions of the attempt count and the policy configuration, so
00012| the scheduler stays fully deterministic.
00013| """
00014| 
00015| from __future__ import annotations
00016| 
00017| from taskflow.model import ConfigError
00018| 
00019| CONSTANT = "constant"
00020| EXPONENTIAL = "exponential"
00021| 
00022| _BACKOFF_KINDS = frozenset({CONSTANT, EXPONENTIAL})
00023| 
00024| 
00025| class RetryPolicy:
00026|     """Decide whether and when a failed attempt should be retried.
00027| 
00028|     Parameters
00029|     ----------
00030|     max_attempts:
00031|         The total number of attempts permitted, counting the first one. A
00032|         value of ``1`` means "no retries": the first failure is permanent. Must
00033|         be a positive integer.
00034|     backoff:
00035|         Either ``"constant"`` or ``"exponential"``. Constant backoff waits the
00036|         same ``base`` delay before every retry. Exponential backoff waits
00037|         ``base * factor ** (attempts_made - 1)``.
00038|     base:
00039|         The base virtual-time delay applied before a retry. Must be
00040|         non-negative.
00041|     factor:
00042|         The growth factor used only by exponential backoff. Must be >= 1.
00043|     max_delay:
00044|         Optional cap applied to the computed delay so exponential growth cannot
00045|         run away.
00046|     """
00047| 
00048|     __slots__ = ("max_attempts", "backoff", "base", "factor", "max_delay")
00049| 
00050|     def __init__(
00051|         self,
00052|         max_attempts=1,
00053|         backoff=CONSTANT,
00054|         base=0,
00055|         factor=2,
00056|         max_delay=None,
00057|     ):
00058|         self.max_attempts = int(max_attempts)
00059|         if self.max_attempts < 1:
00060|             raise ConfigError("max_attempts must be >= 1")
00061|         if backoff not in _BACKOFF_KINDS:
00062|             raise ConfigError(
00063|                 "unknown backoff strategy: {!r} (expected one of {})".format(
00064|                     backoff, sorted(_BACKOFF_KINDS)
00065|                 )
00066|             )
00067|         self.backoff = backoff
00068|         self.base = int(base)
00069|         if self.base < 0:
00070|             raise ConfigError("backoff base must be >= 0")
00071|         self.factor = int(factor)
00072|         if self.factor < 1:
00073|             raise ConfigError("backoff factor must be >= 1")
00074|         self.max_delay = None if max_delay is None else int(max_delay)
00075|         if self.max_delay is not None and self.max_delay < 0:
00076|             raise ConfigError("max_delay must be >= 0")
00077| 
00078|     def attempts_remaining(self, attempts_made):
00079|         """Return how many attempts are still permitted after ``attempts_made``.
00080| 
00081|         ``attempts_made`` is the number of attempts already completed (so it is
00082|         ``1`` immediately after the first attempt fails). The result is clamped
00083|         at zero and never goes negative.
00084|         """
00085| 
00086|         remaining = self.max_attempts - attempts_made
00087|         return remaining if remaining > 0 else 0
00088| 
00089|     def should_retry(self, attempts_made):
00090|         """Return ``True`` if another attempt is permitted.
00091| 
00092|         Given ``attempts_made`` completed attempts, a retry is allowed while
00093|         the run has not yet exhausted its budget -- that is, while at least one
00094|         attempt still remains. With ``max_attempts == 3`` this yields
00095|         ``should_retry(1) is True``, ``should_retry(2) is True`` and
00096|         ``should_retry(3) is False``: the third attempt is the last one, after
00097|         which the failure becomes permanent.
00098|         """
00099| 
00100|         return attempts_made < self.max_attempts - 1
00101| 
00102|     def is_permanent_failure(self, attempts_made):
00103|         """Return ``True`` if a failure after ``attempts_made`` attempts is final."""
00104| 
00105|         return not self.should_retry(attempts_made)
00106| 
00107|     def next_delay(self, attempts_made):
00108|         """Return the virtual-time delay before the next attempt.
00109| 
00110|         For constant backoff this is always ``base``. For exponential backoff
00111|         it is ``base * factor ** (attempts_made - 1)`` -- so the delay after the
00112|         first failure is ``base``, after the second ``base * factor``, and so
00113|         on -- capped at ``max_delay`` when configured.
00114|         """
00115| 
00116|         if attempts_made < 1:
00117|             attempts_made = 1
00118|         if self.backoff == CONSTANT:
00119|             delay = self.base

00121|             delay = self.base * (self.factor ** (attempts_made - 1))
00122|         if self.max_delay is not None and delay > self.max_delay:
00123|             delay = self.max_delay
00124|         return delay
00125| 
00126|     def describe(self):
00127|         """Return a human-readable one-line description of the policy."""
00128| 
00129|         if self.backoff == CONSTANT:
00130|             shape = "constant {}".format(self.base)
00131|         else:
00132|             shape = "exponential base={} factor={}".format(
00133|                 self.base, self.factor
00134|             )

00136|             self.max_attempts, shape
00137|         )

00143|             "max_attempts": self.max_attempts,
00144|             "backoff": self.backoff,

00154|         """Build a policy from a plain dictionary, ignoring unknown keys."""

"""Retry policies for failed job attempts.

A :class:`RetryPolicy` answers two questions the scheduler asks whenever an
attempt fails:

1. *Should we try again?* -- :meth:`RetryPolicy.should_retry`, given how many
   attempts have already been made.
2. *If so, how long until the next attempt?* -- :meth:`RetryPolicy.next_delay`,
   a virtual-time delay derived from the configured backoff strategy.

Both are pure functions of the attempt count and the policy configuration, so
the scheduler stays fully deterministic.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from taskflow.model import ConfigError

CONSTANT = "constant"
EXPONENTIAL = "exponential"
